Q: C Syntax Parsing Only A:

My main question is I'm really trying to understand the difference between semantic structure and syntactic structure. I wanted to see what types of programs would be rejected at the parsing stage if they had some sort of identifier/type ambiguity. It's a bit misleading to me how the C typedef problem is considered ambiguity, because I was thinking it would be 'unambiguous' if I simply coalesced any sort of possibly ambiguous type / identifier reference into some sort of 'ambiguous' node in my AST, and later resolved the actual semantics meaning. But it seems like for some reason the underlying assumption I've found in all my reading is that they insist on calling this syntactic structure and producing two different 'syntax trees' for it, right at that particular instance. To me, the reading of the statement (t)+e can be made into one sort of "syntactic node", and later assigned a semantic interpretation based on if t were a type or an identifier, and I'm trying to understand how come people insist this is crucially syntactic structure.

Q: What does constitute one character for regcomp? Which multibyte encoding does determine this? A:

Each Unicode codepoint constitutes a “character” for this purpose, even in a multi-byte encoding such as UTF-8. POSIX-2024 specifies (emphasis added):

Regular expressions are a context-independent syntax that can represent a wide variety of character sets and character set orderings, where these character sets are interpreted according to the current locale.

The Base Definitions say that a UTF-8 codepoint (if supported) counts as a single “character”:

A sequence of one or more bytes representing a member of a character set. [...]

This term [“character”] corresponds to the ISO C standard term multi-byte character

The document this references, ISO/IEC 9899:2023, defines “multibyte character” as a

sequence of one or more bytes representing a member of the extended character set [...]

Where the “extended character set” is ISO 10646/Unicode or some superset of it.

The specification of Regular Expressions (linked above) then says of the bracket expression you were asking about:

A bracket expression (an expression enclosed in square brackets, "[]") is an RE that shall match a specific set of single characters, and may match a specific set of multi-character collating elements, based on the non-empty set of list expressions contained in the bracket expression.

And:

When a multi-character collating element in a bracket expression is involved, the longest sequence shall be measured in characters consumed from the string to be matched; that is, the collating element counts not as one element, but as the number of characters it matches.

The example given of a collating element was a ch ligature used to sort strings in Spanish alphabetical order.

Character classes are additionally specified to follow LC_CTYPE categories. If you call setlocale( LC_ALL, "" ), the LC_ALL environment variable overrides LC_CTYPE, which overrides LANG. Therefore, if you want to set any category individually, such as LC_TIME or LC_NUMERIC, you need to set the LANG variable, rather than LC_ALL. It makes no sense to combine UTF-8 and non-UTF-8 locale categories (which might produce invalid UTF-8 strings). Therefore, you would normally export LANG to a UTF-8 locale, one or more categories to a different UTF-8 locale, and never need to set LC_CTYPE or LC_ALL.

The language[_territory][.codeset] format for locale names is recommended by POSIX and supported by GNU libc. lowercase ISO 639 language codes and uppercase two-letter ISO 3166 territory codes are the de facto standard. Mainstream OSes including Windows 10 and 11 now understand ru_RU.UTF-8. However, the locale might or might not be installed at runtime, so you should check the return value of setlocale(LC_ALL, "") for error, and might want to fall back on en_US.UTF-8, which should also work for this purpose, if that fails.

Since it is possible for the user to select a non-UTF-8 locale, you may want to check for this as well. On Linux (and most UNIX dialects), you can test

strcmp(nl_langinfo(CODESET), "UTF-8") == 0

Windows 10/11 allows you to set the locale to ".UTF-8", for the user’s preferred language and settings along with the UTF-8 character set.

The GNU C library documents some very minor differences in section 7.6 of its manual.. These should not be visible to your application.

Q: Why GCC produces -Wreduntant-move here? A:

When should std::move be used on a function return value? explains this in much more detail where you'll see when the std::move is superfluous. See this answer for example that says:

The move is unnecessary in both cases. In the second case, std::move is superfluous because you are returning a local variable by value, and the compiler will understand that since you're not going to use that local variable anymore, it can be moved from rather than being copied.

Q: Run/Debug my main.cpp in CLion rebuilds a main executable and runs/debugs it, instead of using the cmake-build-default profile it can build A:

My menu bar was offering to me to Run main.app or Debug main.app, a single source file of my project, instead of Run beaufort-tempete and Debug beaufort-tempete, the executable.

This I've understood when without clue, eventually I've decided to leave CLion, delete its .idea folder, and restart it.
It restarted with its Run/Debug entries in the menu bar corrected → maybe, my CLion environment was corrupted.

Whatever, starting a CLion project with a conda env used this way is somewhat hard...
Yet the key to make it working seems to be:

  1. in Build, Execution, Deployment, create your toolchain that uses the conda env with the due cc, c++ and cmake, and put it on the top of the list: it's essential.

  2. Quit CLion, delete the .idea folder

  3. Restart it. It will understand now where it is, and set itself more correctly.

But you can see how things are unsteady here...
I'll try to find a better solution trough a Cmake Preset.

Q: Why does a class inherited from lambda type lack conversion to function pointer in Visual C++? A:

The program is well-formed and msvc is wrong to reject the program, as explained below.

First, from expr.prim.lambda#8:

The closure type for a non-generic lambda-expression with no lambda-capture whose constraints (if any) are satisfied has a conversion function to pointer to function with C++ language linkage having the same parameter and return types as the closure type's function call operator. The conversion is to “pointer to noexcept function” if the function call operator has a non-throwing exception specification. If the function call operator is a static member function, then the value returned by this conversion function is the address of the function call operator. Otherwise, the value returned by this conversion function is the address of a function F that, when invoked, has the same effect as invoking the closure type's function call operator on a default-constructed instance of the closure type. F is a constexpr function if the function call operator is a constexpr function and is an immediate function if the function call operator is an immediate function.

This means that L already has a non-static conversion function that returns the address of such a function F which when invoked has the effect of invoking L's function call operator.

Next, since A inherits from L, it will also inherit the above mentioned conversion function as per class.derived:

Members of a base class are also members of the derived class.

Basically, we don't need to define/declare the conversion function again in the derived class as it is already a member of derived class.

Here is the newly submitted msvc bug:

https://developercommunity.visualstudio.com/t/MSVC-rejects-valid-program-involving-inh/11040924

Q: Eclipse 2021-09 is not showing outline for javascript files A:

I am using Eclipse IDE for Enterprise Java and Web Developers (includes Incubating components) Version: 2023-03 (4.27.0) Build id: 20230309-1520 OS: Windows 11.

Your recent edit on "LanguageServer not initialized after 10s" reminded me that I had disabled the Language Server from running in the background, as it was constantly bugging me. I went ahead and started it, this time only for Javascript content types.

Windows -> Preferences -> Language Servers

Thereafter, my outline started appearing.

Q: How to send telethon message with non telegram event triggers A:

You would need to use events to do that. the event for clicking on a button is events.CallbackQuery

An example code would be as follow :

from telethon import events
from telethon.tl.custom import Button

@client.on(events.CallbackQuery)
async def handler(event):
    await event.answer('You clicked {}!'.format(event.data))

client.send_message(chat, 'Pick one', buttons=[
    [Button.inline('Left'), Button.inline('Right')]]
])

you can find more examples here: https://github.com/LonamiWebs/Telethon/tree/v1/telethon_examples
